0.name: completed
0.meaning: The command did what it was asked. For a run, every loop it includes is completed.
0.next: Nothing. A run's results are in each loop's outputs/ folder.

1.name: error
1.meaning: Something went wrong that no other code covers, for example an export that could not be written.
1.next: Read the message devloops printed; it names what failed.

2.name: usage error
2.meaning: The command was not usable as given: an unknown option, a missing value, no project found, or an invalid run configuration. Nothing was changed.
2.next: Fix the command or the configuration file the message names, then run it again.

10.name: awaiting-approval
10.meaning: The run paused for you: a plan is waiting for review, or a question has no suggested answer.
10.next: Review the plan, then run devloops approve, or devloops replan with your feedback.

20.name: stopped-on-failure
20.meaning: The run stopped: a milestone used all its trials, the plan could not be made, a question needs your answer, or the run reached its limit of calls to Claude Code.
20.next: Run devloops status to see why. Then devloops retry to grant more trials, or change the requirements and start again.

30.name: stopped-on-input-error
30.meaning: Something the run needs is missing or wrong: the requirements, a story, a tool, the target folder, the project configuration, or an input that changed since the run started. devloops check and devloops init also exit 30 when they find a problem.
30.next: Fix what the message names, then run the same command again.

40.name: lock held
40.meaning: Another devloops command is working in this workspace, or one that ended abruptly left its lock behind.
40.next: Wait for the other command to finish. If none is running, run devloops status, which says how to clear the lock.

50.name: stopped-on-service-error
50.meaning: Claude Code could not be used: the service was unavailable, a rate limit was reached, or authentication failed. No trial was used up.
50.next: Wait, or log in to Claude Code again, then run devloops run to resume.

130.name: interrupted
130.meaning: You pressed Ctrl+C. What was already recorded is kept.
130.next: Run devloops run to resume; devloops status shows where the run stands.

steps.plan: Reads the requirements and the target and writes the plan: milestones in order, each with its tasks, acceptance criteria and how to start the application. It changes no files.
steps.replan: Writes the plan again, taking your answers in open-questions.md into account, when you run devloops replan. It changes no files.
steps.implement: A milestone's first trial: Claude Code writes the code for the milestone's tasks in the target.
steps.fix: Each later trial of a milestone: Claude Code is shown why the previous trial failed and changes the code to fix it.
steps.author-checks: Before any code is written for a backend milestone, writes the HTTP requests and expected answers that will check it. The checks are then kept unchanged for every trial.
steps.validate-ui: Checks a frontend milestone in a real browser: Claude Code drives the browser through each acceptance criterion and reports what it saw, with screenshots as evidence.

run.running: A devloops command is working on the run's loops.
run.paused: A loop is waiting for you to review its plan or answer a question.
run.stopped: A loop stopped, or the command was interrupted. Running devloops run again resumes it.
run.completed: Every loop the run includes is completed.

loop.not-started: The loop has no run in this workspace yet.
loop.planning: The plan step is writing the plan.
loop.awaiting-approval: The plan is written and waits for your review.
loop.implementing: The plan is approved and milestones are being built, one at a time.
loop.completed: Every milestone of the plan is achieved.
loop.stopped-on-failure: The loop stopped because something failed: a milestone ran out of trials, the plan could not be made, a question needs an answer, or the call limit was reached.
loop.stopped-on-input-error: The loop stopped because an input is missing, wrong, or changed.
loop.stopped-on-service-error: The loop stopped because Claude Code could not be used. Running again resumes where it was.

milestone.in-progress: A trial is building or validating it.
milestone.achieved: A trial passed validation. It is never run again.
milestone.failed: Every allowed trial failed. A retry grant sets it back to in-progress.

task.implemented: Claude Code reports it done; validation has not confirmed it yet.
task.failed: Its milestone ran out of trials before the task was achieved.

trial.in-progress: Claude Code is working, or devloops is validating the result.
trial.failed: Validation failed, or the call failed in a way that counts against the milestone.
trial.void: The trial did not count, for example because Claude Code was unavailable. It uses up no trial.

approval.approve: You approved the plan with devloops approve.
approval.replan: You asked for a new plan with devloops replan.
approval.auto-approve: devloops approved the plan by itself and accepted Claude's suggested answers (questions: accept-suggested).

stop_reasons.trials-exhausted: A milestone used all its trials without passing validation.
stop_reasons.planning-trials-exhausted: The plan step did not produce a usable plan within its trials.
stop_reasons.invocation-cap: The run reached its limit of calls to Claude Code (max_invocations_per_run).
stop_reasons.needs-input: Claude Code asked a question that needs your answer before the work can go on.
stop_reasons.missing-input: A file the run needs, such as the requirements, is missing or empty.
stop_reasons.story-not-found: The story named with --story-id is not in the requirements.
stop_reasons.invalid-api-spec: The OpenAPI document the frontend loop builds against is not a valid OpenAPI document.
stop_reasons.missing-tool: A program the loop needs is not installed: Claude Code, curl, or the Playwright MCP server.
stop_reasons.input-changed: An input the run started with, such as the requirements or the plan, changed since.
stop_reasons.workspace-mismatch: The workspace belongs to another target or project than the one given.
stop_reasons.target-unwritable: The target folder cannot be created or written to.
stop_reasons.service-unavailable: Claude Code's service did not answer.
stop_reasons.rate-limited: Claude Code refused calls for a while because too many were made.
stop_reasons.auth-failed: Claude Code is not logged in, or its login expired.
stop_reasons.interrupted: The run was stopped with Ctrl+C while planning or implementing; running again resumes it.

files.<loop>/outputs/final-report.md: The loop's final report, written when every milestone is achieved: what was built and what each milestone's validation showed.
files.<loop>/outputs/milestone-<NN>-<slug>.md: One milestone of the plan, readable: its goal, tasks and acceptance criteria.
files.<loop>/outputs/open-questions.md: The plan's open questions, with Claude's suggested answers. You write your answers here before approving.
files.<loop>/outputs/openapi.json: The backend's OpenAPI document, published after each achieved milestone with only the operations validation called.
files.<loop>/outputs/plan-summary.md: The plan in one page, for review before approval.
files.<loop>/progress.md: Where the loop stands: each milestone, its status and its trials. Rewritten as the run goes.
A copy of one call's Claude Code conversation (its transcript), kept so it can be read later.
files.<loop>/state/events.jsonl: One line per thing that happened in the loop, in order: run started, plan stored, trial started, validation passed or failed, and so on.
files.<loop>/state/invocations.jsonl: One line per call to Claude Code: its step, milestone and trial, when it ran, its tokens and cost, and how it ended.
files.<loop>/state/milestones/<id>/checks.json: A backend milestone's checks: the HTTP requests and expected answers written before any code, kept unchanged for every trial.
files.<loop>/state/milestones/<id>/trials/<n>/: The body of the answer a check's HTTP request got.
The exact curl command a check ran.
The headers of the answer a check's HTTP request got.
The body a check sent with its HTTP request.
What the application printed while it ran for this trial's validation.
One trial: its kind (implement or fix), its status, the calls it made, the assumptions and questions Claude reported, and why it failed, if it did.
What validation found for one trial: each check and acceptance criterion, passed or failed, with its evidence.
files.<loop>/state/plan.json: The plan: the milestones in order, their tasks and acceptance criteria, and how to start the application.
files.<loop>/state/prompts/<seq>-<step>.md: The exact prompt one call sent to Claude Code, with secrets replaced by ***.
files.<loop>/state/prompts/<seq>-<step>.settin: The Claude Code settings one call ran with: the hooks that keep writes inside the target and stop Claude from ending processes by name.
files.<loop>/state/run.json: The loop's run: its status and why it stopped, its inputs, the settings it started with, the approval, and each milestone's progress.
files.<loop>/state/run.log: Every progress line the loop printed, whatever --quiet or --verbose said.
files.<loop>/task.md: The run's inputs in one page: the requirements, the target folder and the settings in effect.
files.exports/<stamp>.html: A dashboard export: the whole dashboard in one file, written by devloops dashboard --export.
files.run/progress.md: Where the whole run stands: each loop and its status.
files.run/state.json: The run across its loops: its status, each loop's step, and the handoff from the backend loop to the frontend loop.
files.workspace.json: The workspace's identity: its name, the requirements it was started with, the target folder of each loop, and its configuration file.
